risks: Low: bedside tests and an exercise test, which carries a small risk of adverse events and is supervised by trained staff; no change to prehabilitation allocation during the study.
consent: Written consent at pre-assessment for the bedside tests and for exercise testing within two weeks; declining does not affect care.
data: Study database holds test results and a study number; linked to the surgical record only for eligibility.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older, frail and disabled patients and patients with limited English are most likely to be unable to complete tests or to be misclassified. Interpreters are offered, test instructions are demonstrated, and accuracy is reported for patients aged 75 and over and by frailty.
effectiveness: A validated bedside test would let prehabilitation start earlier for the patients who need it.
efficiency: Uses existing physiotherapy and exercise test staff.
grants: None needed; a later triage comparison could seek funding.
partnerships: Physiotherapy, exercise physiology, the surgical pre-assessment team and two patient partners who completed prehabilitation.
rebPath: Submitted to the REB on 2026-09-05 under ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles; the committee meets on 2026-10-20, so approval is unknown and recruitment waits for it.
limitations: One centre; prevalence may differ from planning; blinding depends on sequencing.
summary: Low-risk accuracy study with consent; REB decision pending.
